text:
Lynn Conway was a pioneering figure in VLSI technology, known for her work on the Mead–Conway VLSI design methodology and the MOSIS prototype. Her contributions fostered the growth of the electronic design automation industry, established the foundry model for chip design, and spurred technology startups in the 1980s and 1990s. She also coined the term "Conway effect" to describe how societal bias overlooks innovations from marginalized groups.
Beyond her technical achievements, Conway was actively involved in transgender rights activism. She began sharing her story publicly in 1999, detailing her gender transition, and later advocated for equal employment protections for transgender individuals in the high-technology industry. She was honored with numerous accolades, including the Electronics 1981 Award for Achievement and the Computer Pioneer Award from the IEEE Computer Society in 2009.
